???+ remember "Before you start, remember"

    ??? question "What does a warp do when its lanes disagree about a branch?"

        It runs both sides, one after the other, with the lanes that did not choose the side currently running masked off. A branch on a value that is the same in every lane costs one pass, because every lane makes the same choice.

        Introduced in [A. The machine: G2. The SIMT execution model](g2-simt.md).

    ??? question "How does SIMT differ from SIMD?"

        A SIMD instruction exposes its width to the software, which must pack data and handle masks itself. A SIMT program describes one thread, and the hardware runs 32 of them together and masks lanes when they disagree.

        Introduced in [A. The machine: G2. The SIMT execution model](g2-simt.md).

    ??? question "What is a warp, and how many threads does one NVIDIA warp or Apple SIMD-group hold?"

        A fixed-size group of threads that the GPU issues one instruction to at a time; each thread is one of the warp's lanes. It is 32 threads wide on NVIDIA GPUs and on Apple GPUs.

        Introduced in [A. The machine: G2. The SIMT execution model](g2-simt.md).
